In SQL Server 2025, declare a native document column with ConfigSettings {{c1::JSON}} NOT NULL.
column2:
The type is generally available. Azure SQL Managed Instance requires the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy.
Review source

column1: The native SQL Server json type stores documents in a {{c1::binary}} format.
column2:
The stored document is already parsed for more efficient property access.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server 2016 through 2022, a common column type for storing JSON text is {{c1::NVARCHAR(MAX)}}.
column2:
These versions have JSON functions but not the native json data type.
Review source

column1: At the document root, the native SQL Server json type accepts {{c1::an object or an array}}.
column2:
A bare JSON number, string, boolean, or JSON null is not a valid native json document.
Review source

column1: For non-NULL JSON text, CHECK ({{c1::ISJSON}}(ConfigSettings) = 1) rejects malformed documents.
column2:
Without a type argument, ISJSON accepts JSON objects or arrays rather than bare scalars.
Review source

column1: The path {{c1::$}} refers to a JSON document's root.
column2:
For an object or array document, JSON_QUERY(ConfigSettings, '$') returns the whole document as JSON text.
Review source

column1: Read length inside a dimensions object with JSON_VALUE(Attributes, '{{c1::$.dimensions.length}}').
column2:
Each dot selects a nested property in the path.
Review source

column1: Without RETURNING, JSON_VALUE returns a SQL value of type {{c1::NVARCHAR(4000)}}.
column2:
Convert the result when a numeric or other specific SQL type is required.
Review source

column1: For a native json column in SQL Server 2025, use UPDATE dbo.ConfigurationData SET ConfigSettings.{{c1::modify}}('$.theme', 'light') WHERE ConfigID = 1;
column2:
This method can perform in-place updates when the replacement value fits.
Review source

column1: For an NVARCHAR(MAX) JSON column, use UPDATE dbo.ConfigurationData SET ConfigSettings = {{c1::JSON_MODIFY}}(ConfigSettings, '$.theme', 'light') WHERE ConfigID = 1;
column2:
Assign the returned JSON text back to the column to store the update.
Review source

column1: Write JSON false rather than numeric zero with JSON_MODIFY(ConfigSettings, '$.notifications', CAST(0 AS {{c1::BIT}})).
column2:
The SQL value's type determines whether JSON stores a boolean or a number.
Review source

column1: With ThemeValue defined as an indexable computed column, use {{c1::CREATE INDEX}} IX_Theme ON dbo.ConfigurationData(ThemeValue);
column2:
This creates a standard index over the extracted property, not over the entire JSON document.
Review source

column1: For a NOT NULL JSON column Attributes, require weight with CHECK (JSON_PATH_EXISTS(Attributes, '$.weight') = {{c1::1}}).
column2:
This checks that the path exists, not that weight contains a valid numeric value.
Review source

column1: On an eligible SQL Server 2025 table with a native json column, use {{c1::CREATE JSON INDEX}} IX_Settings ON dbo.ConfigurationData(ConfigSettings);
column2:
The base table must have a clustered primary key.
Review source

column1: A native json column cannot be a {{c1::key column}} of a standard B-tree index.
column2:
Index an extracted property, or use a dedicated JSON index on the native column.
Review source

column1: Indexing a suitable JSON_VALUE computed column does not require the {{c1::PERSISTED}} keyword.
column2:
The nonclustered index stores the extracted key values.
Review source
